title: Feshbach open/closed-channel optical Hamiltonian with degenerate closed-channel resolvent
expression_sketch: Orthogonal projectors P + Q = I, P**2 = P, Q**2 = Q, PQ = 0. Coupled Schrödinger: P H P |P> + P H Q |Q> = E |P>, Q H P |P> + Q H Q |Q> = E |Q>. Closed-channel solve: |Q> = (E - Q H Q)**(-1) Q H P |P>. Effective open-channel Hamiltonian: H_eff(E) = P H P + P H Q * (E - Q H Q)**(-1) * Q H P, acting in P-space with H_eff(E)|P> = E|P>. Magnetic two-channel specialisation (ultracold Feshbach resonance): scattering length a(B) = a_bg * (1 - Delta/(B - B0)), pole when the closed-channel bound energy matches the open-channel threshold. Isolated-resonance member is the Breit-Wigner pole of the optical potential; overlapping resonances are the same meromorphic family.
latent_structure: Energy-dependent optical Hamiltonian obtained by Schur-complementing the closed-channel block. The closed-channel resolvent (E - QHQ)**(-1) is the master kernel; open-channel dynamics, isolated Feshbach poles, and the magnetic scattering-length pole a ~ 1/(B-B0) are members. Degenerate denominator when E hits spec(QHQ) or B hits B0. Not CSE of PHP and PHQ, and not Lippmann-Schwinger 1/(E-H0 +/- i epsilon).

E.notes: total energy of the two-channel Schrödinger problem as written

B.notes: magnetic field in the ultracold specialisation

B0.notes: resonance field in a = a_bg (1 - Delta/(B-B0))

function_domains.a: s-wave scattering length as a function of magnetic field
function_domains.V_D: closed-channel potential curve admitting a bound state of energy E_D

nonzero_conditions.statement: Magnetic scattering length is written with denominator B - B0
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Wikipedia Feshbach resonance, Magnetic Feshbach resonance: a = a_bg (1 - Delta/(B - B0))

nonzero_conditions.statement: Closed-channel elimination writes (E - QHQ)**(-1), i.e. E is not an eigenvalue of QHQ in the formal solve
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Feshbach projection algebra as written in the two-channel block elimination (Feshbach, Ann. Phys. 5 (1958) 357; 19 (1962) 287); lecture restatement H_eff(E) = H_PP + H_PQ (E - H_QQ)**(-1) H_QP

analytic_domains.statement: An energetically accessible reaction channel is open; a channel forbidden by energy conservation is closed
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Feshbach resonance, Introduction: 'An energetically accessible reaction channel is referred to as an open channel, whereas a reaction channel forbidden by energy conservation is referred to as a closed channel'

analytic_domains.statement: A Feshbach resonance occurs when the closed-channel bound energy E_D is approximately the open-channel energy T + V_c(R) + Delta(P)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Feshbach resonance: E_D ≈ T + V_c(R) + Delta(P_0) for some parameter range {P_0}

analytic_domains.statement: Feshbach 1958: the generalised optical potential has poles that give rise to resonances; its real and imaginary parts satisfy a dispersion-type relation
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Feshbach, H., Ann. Phys. 5 (1958) 357-390, abstract: 'The real and imaginary part of this potential satisfy a dispersion type relation while its poles give rise to resonances in nuclear reactions'

analytic_domains.statement: Magnetic specialisation: a(B) = a_bg (1 - Delta/(B - B0)), with B0 the field at which resonance occurs
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Wikipedia Feshbach resonance, Magnetic Feshbach resonance

branch_conventions: P selects open-channel components; Q selects closed-channel components, as in Feshbach 1962: 'the projection operator which selects the open channel components of the wave function'.
The magnetic formula is the ultracold two-channel specialisation of the same closed-channel pole, not a separate object.

limit_domains.statement: Feshbach 1958 isolates a single resonance and also extends the derivation to overlapping resonances; both are poles of the same optical potential
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: Feshbach, Ann. Phys. 5 (1958) 357-390, abstract: 'A new derivation of the Breit-Wigner formula... extended to the case of overlapping resonances'

source_provenance: Feshbach, H., Unified theory of nuclear reactions, Ann. Phys. 5 (1958) 357-390, doi:10.1016/0003-4916(58)90007-1
Feshbach, H., A unified theory of nuclear reactions. II, Ann. Phys. 19 (1962) 287-313, doi:10.1016/0003-4916(62)90221-X

derived_conditions.statement: When Q is closed (energy conservation forbids Q), the formal inverse (E - QHQ)**(-1) is the closed-channel propagator appearing in H_eff
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Block elimination of the Q-component of the two-channel Schrödinger equation together with Wikipedia's closed-channel definition

public_source: Wikipedia, Feshbach resonance (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feshbach_resonance); Feshbach, Ann. Phys. 5 (1958) 357-390, doi:10.1016/0003-4916(58)90007-1; Feshbach, Ann. Phys. 19 (1962) 287-313, doi:10.1016/0003-4916(62)90221-X.
why_not_cse_lgg: CSE can share H_PQ. LGG antiunifies two coupled-channel blocks. The scientific object is an energy-dependent Schur complement whose closed-channel resolvent poles are the Feshbach resonances, including the magnetic 1/(B-B0) member.
proposer_leak_risk: Do not plant 'optical potential', 'Schur complement', or 'Feshbach' as gold names. Do not import Lippmann-Schwinger +/- i epsilon as a gold regularisation; closed-channel invertibility is the written domain here.
notes: Not Lippmann-Schwinger (ac-r07). Not Kato simple eigenvalue. Open vs closed is written on Wikipedia; magnetic pole B=B0 is written without a folklore i epsilon. Feshbach's E(+)=E+i eta bookkeeping for open channels inside Q is not inserted: the packaged identity is the closed-Q Schur complement plus the written magnetic formula. is_guo=false.
